en: Having bowed to Narayana, and to Nara the best of men, and to the goddess Sarasvati, one should then speak the word of victory.
Victory to Vyasa, son of Parashara, the joy of Satyavati's heart, from whose lotus mouth the world drinks the nectar of speech.
I bow to Madhava, the supreme joy, whose grace makes the mute eloquent and the lame cross a mountain.

May the Bharata lotus, which is the speech of Vyasa, son of Parashara, bring us good. It is spotless, rich with the fragrance of the Gita's meaning, with many tales as its filaments, opened by the telling of Hari's stories, and drunk joyfully day after day by good people like bees. May it destroy the stain of the Kali age.
One who gives a hundred cows with golden horns to a Brahmin learned in the Vedas and well versed in scripture, and one who hears the whole holy tale of the Bhavishya, gain equal merit, each of them.
Having composed all the Puranas, many and pleasing, the son of Parashara then wrote, for his own happiness, all that will happen in the Kali age, the duties of the future.
Among these, Vyasa briefly told the future, together with the teachings, rules of duty and traditions composed by Parashara and other sages, the foremost of all seers.
Seeing that people were short-lived, without learning, and behaving like animals, Vyasa composed the renowned Purana for their happiness and understanding.

Victory to the sun, lamp of the world and maker of the worlds. Victory to the dark-bodied Murari, bearer of the Sharnga bow. Victory to the god named Rudra, who wears the moon on his head. Victory to that radiant god, the shining one of brilliant rays.
All the great sages came to see the mighty King Shatanika, who was surrounded by splendour.
They were Bhrigu, Atri, Vasishtha, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu, and likewise Parashara, Vyasa, Sumantu and Jaimini.
The sage Paila, Yajnavalkya, the great ascetic Gautama, the wise sage Bharadvaja, and likewise Narada and Parvata.
The great Vaishampayana, the great ascetic Shaunaka, Daksha, Angiras, Garga, and the great ascetic Galava.
Seeing the sages arrived, the wise King Shatanika went to meet them and honoured them as the rules direct.

first: पुरोहितं पुरस्कृत्य अर्ध्यं गां स्वागतेन च ।
en: With his family priest in front, he honoured them all with water of welcome, a cow and words of greeting, and bowed deeply with his head.
When they were comfortably seated, free of fear and weariness, the king bowed to them, raised his right arm, and spoke.

first: इदानीं सफलं जन्म मन्येऽहं भुवि सत्तमाः ।
en: O best of men, I think my birth is fruitful today on earth, and so are my fame, glory and strength, O tigers among the twice-born.

first: धन्योऽहं पुण्यकर्मा च यतो मां द्रष्टुमागताः ।
en: I am blessed and have done holy deeds, since you have come to see me. By merely remembering you, a person is purified.
I wish to hear some supreme teaching of duty, based on kindness, O mighty ones.

first: येनाहं धर्मशास्त्रं तु श्रुत्वा गच्छे परां गतिम् ।
en: By hearing this teaching of duty, may I reach the highest state, as my father did when he heard the Bharata long ago.
When the king had said this, those Brahmins gathered on every side, and after discussing it closely among themselves,
they honoured Vyasa and said these words: "O lord, please win over Vyasa; he will tell you."
"While he is here, O mighty-armed one, we cannot speak. How can a student speak when his teacher is present, O wise one?"
"He is always our teacher, Narayana himself, and he is kind and knows the divine rules."
"He has spoken the teaching of duty, complete with dharma and the rest, to purify all four classes of great souls."
"People fear a deep scripture as a sick man fears medicine. The sage himself has told the Bharata in great length."

first: यथा स्वादु च पथ्यं च दद्यास्त्वं भिषगौषधम् ।
en: "As a physician would give medicine that is both tasty and healthful, so the sage made the Bharata both pleasing and useful."
"This Bharata is called the ladder of climbing faith. Hearing it, people see heaven and hell as if before their eyes."
"The truth about gods, holy places and austerities is settled by the Bharata alone. Even the Mimamsa teachers cannot make a person an unbeliever once he knows it."

first: विष्णौ देवेषु वेदेषु गुरुषु ब्राह्मणेषु च ।
en: "Devotion to Vishnu, the gods, the Vedas, teachers and Brahmins comes, bringing good, to the wise through the Bharata alone."
"From the Bharata come success in duty, wealth, desire and liberation. The Bharata is a straight path for those going to the state of nirvana."
"The full range of liberation, duty, wealth and desire is set out in the Bharata. Those tormented by the impermanence of things are freed by it."
"Hearing from the Bharata of the downfall of the glory of the Vrishnis and Pandavas, a wise person, O best of kings, takes refuge in merit, since suffering ends."

first: एवंविधं भारतं वै प्रोक्तं येन महात्मना ।
en: "The great soul who spoke such a Bharata is Narayana himself, the great sage in the form of Vyasa."

first: स तेषां वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रतापी यो महीपतिः ।
en: Hearing their words, the mighty king won over the sage Vyasa, who was skilled in the scriptures.
I have folded my hands and bowed my head at your feet, O Brahmin. Tell me the teaching of duty, by which I may become pure.
Lift me out of this worldly existence by telling a holy tale, as my father did in the past by telling the Bharata.
Hearing his words, Vyasa replied: "This pupil of mine, Sumantu, will tell you, O lord."
"What you wish, O mighty-armed one, he will tell: something pleasing, wonderful and good to hear, O tiger among the Bharatas, which takes away the fear of all sins."
"It is like the explanation of the Mahabharata that Vaishampayana once told your father, which removes the sin of killing a Brahmin."
Then all the sages said to the king: "O mighty-armed one, Vyasa of boundless wisdom has spoken well."
"Ask Sumantu, royal sage, who is skilled in all scriptures. We too, O king, feel a wish to hear." Then the radiant Vyasa said to the sage Sumantu:

first: कथयास्मै कथास्तात! याः श्रुत्वा मोदते नृपः ।
en: "Tell him the tales, my dear, by hearing which the king may be delighted, tales of the Bharata and others in which his mind delights."
The radiant Sumantu too, hearing the wish of the wise Vyasa and of all the sages,

first: चकार वक्तुं स मनस्तस्मै राज्ञे महामतिः ।
en: the wise one made up his mind to speak to the king, at the command of Vyasa and of all the sages, O Brahmin.
Then the radiant king, descendant of Ajamidha, bowed deeply to the best of the twice-born and began to speak.
O Brahmin, tell me a holy tale to purify me, hearing which, O best of Brahmins, I may be freed from all sins.
There are many kinds of scriptures, O descendant of Bharata, hearing which a person is freed from all sins, O king.

first: किमिच्छसि महाबाहो! श्रोतुं यत्त्वां ब्रवीमि वै ।
en: What do you wish to hear, O mighty-armed one, from the tales of the Bharata and others, in which duty and the rest are established?
Which are the books of duty, O best of Brahmins, of good vows, hearing which a person is freed from all sins?
Listen to the books of duty: Manu, Vishnu, Yama, Angiras, Vasishtha, Daksha, Samvarta, Shatatapa and Parashara,
Apastamba, Ushanas, Katyayana, Brihaspati, Gautama, Shankha and Likhita, Harita, and Atri.

first: एतानि धर्मशास्त्राणि श्रुत्वा ज्ञात्वा च भारत! ।
en: O descendant of Bharata, one who hears and knows these books of duty goes to the city of the gods and rejoices there, without doubt.
The books of duty you have named, O Brahmin of good vows, I do not wish to hear; I have already heard them.
They are said by the learned for the three classes, but not for the good of the Shudras. Hear my words on this.
What is for the good of all four classes here, O good Brahmin, is heard in the three worlds.
And especially for the fourth class, O best of the twice-born. (text unclear)
The Vedas are meant for the three classes beginning with Brahmins, and the books of Manu and others, and the Vedangas on every side.
The Shudras, O lord of the twice-born, seem very wretched. How could they be praised in matters of duty, wealth, desire and liberation?

first: आगमेन विहीना हि अहो कष्टं मतं मम् ।
en: Without a sacred text they are lost; I think this is sad. What text did the wise twice-born say long ago for them? Tell me, O Brahmin, how they may gain the three aims of life and the good of both.

first: साधु साधु महाबाहो! शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
en: Well said, well said, O mighty-armed one. Hear my excellent answer. I will tell of those books that are said to be for the good of all four classes.
Listen to those books of duty, O best of kings, which the wise have declared especially purifying for the Shudras.
They are the eighteen Puranas and the story of Rama, descendant of Raghu, O tiger of the Kurus, for success in duty, desire and wealth.
And the Bharata, O hero, was told by the wise son of Parashara, joining the whole meaning of the Vedas with the books of duty.
The kind sage made this scripture for the good of the four classes here; for those sunk in worldly existence it is the finest boat.
Having mastered the eighteen Puranas and the eight grammars, the son of Satyavati composed the Bharata collection.

first: यां श्रुत्वा पुरुषो राजन्! मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया ।
en: Hearing it, a person, O king, is freed from the sin of killing a Brahmin. The first Purana is called Brahma, the second Indra's.

first: याम्यं प्रोक्तं ततो रौद्रं वायव्यं वारुणं तथा ।
en: Then are named the Yamya, the Raudra, the Vayavya and the Varuna, and likewise the Savitra, and the eighth, the Vaishnava.
Learn from me these grammars and Puranas: Brahma, Padma, Vaishnava, Shaiva, and likewise Bhagavata.
Also the Naradiya and the Markandeya as the seventh, the Agneya as the eighth, O hero, and the Bhavishya is remembered as the ninth.
The tenth is Brahmavaivarta, the Linga is remembered as the eleventh, the Varaha is called the twelfth, and the Skanda the thirteenth.

first: चतुर्दशं वामनं च कौर्मं पञ्चदशं स्मृतम् ।
en: The fourteenth is Vamana, the Kurma is remembered as the fifteenth, then the Matsya, the Garuda, and after that the Brahmanda.
O tiger of the Kurus, these books of duty are said by the learned to be common to all, always for the good of the classes.
They are worth hearing by all four here, O king of good vows. What do you wish to hear of them, O mighty-armed best of kings?

first: भारतं तु श्रुतं विप्र तातस्याङ्कगतेन तु ।
en: I have heard the Bharata, O Brahmin, sitting on my father's lap, and I have heard Rama's story on every side.

first: पुराणानि च विप्रेन्द्र भविष्यं न तु सुव्रत ।
en: And I have heard the Puranas, O best of Brahmins, but not the Bhavishya, O good one. Tell me the Purana, O best of Brahmins; I am curious about the Bhavishya.

first: साधु साधु महाबाहो साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि मानद ।
en: Well said, well said, O mighty-armed one; you have asked well, O giver of honour. Listen as I tell the great ninth Purana.
By hearing it a person is freed from all sins, O king, and having gained the reward of the horse sacrifice he goes to the sun, without doubt.
This supreme teaching of duty was spoken by Brahma. A learned Brahmin should study it with care.
It should be taught to disciples of the four classes. It must not be studied by anyone except a Brahmin or a Kshatriya. A Shudra should only listen, and never study it.
With an image of the god set in front, and with Brahmins, O best of kings, Shudras and other twice-born should only listen to it.

first: श्रौतं स्मार्तं हि वै धर्मं प्रोक्तमस्मिन्नृपोत्तम ।
en: Duty from the Vedas and from the Smriti is told in this, O best of kings. Therefore Shudras should never listen without Brahmins.
A Brahmin of firm vows who studies this scripture is never stained by the faults of deeds born of mind, speech and body.

first: शृण्वन्ति चापि ये राजन् भक्त्या वै ब्राह्मणादयः ।
en: Even Brahmins and others, O king, who listen with devotion are freed from all sins and go to heaven, O lord.
A Brahmin who recites it to all the classes, O best of kings, is called the teacher of all the classes here.
He is to be honoured at all times by all the classes, O ruler of men; even alone he deserves this whole earth.
This is the best blessing, this increases understanding, this always brings fame, this gives the highest good.
In this, duty is told in full, with the good and bad of actions, and the lasting conduct of all four classes.
Right conduct is the first duty, as the Vedas say, O best of men. So a wise twice-born should always be devoted to it.
A Brahmin who falls from right conduct does not gain the fruit of the Vedas; one joined to right conduct is said to receive the full fruit.
Seeing in this way the course of duty through conduct, the sages took conduct as the supreme root of all austerity.

first: अन्ये च मानवा राजन्नाचारं संश्रिता सदा ।
en: Other people too, O king, always rely on conduct. So in this Purana there is praise of right conduct.

first: वृत्तान्तानि च राजेन्द्र तथा चोक्तानि पण्डितैः ।
en: The learned have also told, O best of kings, the accounts of events: the origin of the three worlds, the best rule for the rites of passage, and the way of hearing the histories is taught, O king.
Here, O king, is taught the greatness of the reciter, the vows, the student's discipline, the ways of the stages of life, and the supreme rule for the graduate.
Also marriage and the rules for approaching a wife, the marks of marriages, and the marks of men and women are told here.
The rule for the great sacrifices, the lasting rules of scripture, the marks of the earth, and the fine marks of worshipping gods, my dear.

first: वृत्तीनां लक्षणं चैव स्नातकस्य व्रतानि च ।
en: The marks of livelihoods, the vows of the graduate, what is fit and unfit to eat, purity, and the cleansing of things.
The duty of women, the life of ascetics, liberation and renunciation, the whole duty of a king, and the deciding of cases.
The greatness of the sun, and of holy places, O lord of the people; the greatness of Narayana and of Rudra is told.

first: महाभाग्यं च विप्राणां माहात्म्यं पुस्तकस्य च ।
en: The great fortune of Brahmins, the greatness of the book, the story of the goddess Durga, and of truth, O wise one.
A short summary of the rules, the duties of women and men, the division of property, the duty of gambling, and the testing of storytellers.
The service of Vaishyas and Shudras, the birth of mixed classes, the duty in times of distress for the classes, and the rules of atonement.
The rule of the twilight prayers, purification after death, the rules of bathing and offering water, the rule of the offering to all gods, and the rule of eating, O king.
The marks of the tooth-stick, the fine arrangement of the Vedic schools, and the threefold course through worldly existence born of deeds.
The path to final good, the examination of the good and bad of actions, the marks of wives, and the testing of worthy recipients are told.

first: प्रसूतिं चापि गर्भस्य तथा कर्मफलं नृप ।
en: Also birth from the womb, the fruit of deeds, O king, the duties of caste, family and the Vedas, O ruler.
And the duties of those keeping the Vedic fire vows. The lord Brahma told this to the great-souled Shankara, O best of the Kuru line.
Shankara told it to Vishnu, O joy of the Kurus, and Vishnu again told it to Narada, O lord of the earth.
Indra received it from Narada, Parashara even from Indra, Vyasa from Parashara, and I from Vyasa, O lord.
So this excellent Purana has come down through a line of teachers. You too, O best of kings, hear from me what is supremely good.
All the Puranas should be known, O best of men; the wise say they are twelve thousand verses each.
They have grown again with many tales added, O bull among men. As the Skanda is, so is this Bhavishya, O joy of the Kurus.

first: स्कान्दं शतसहस्रं तु लोकानां ज्ञातमेव हि ।
en: The Skanda is known to have a hundred thousand verses; this Bhavishya was made by the sage at fifty thousand in number.
Hearing this with devotion, a person gains this reward: prosperity, growth and wealth surely come to him.
